content.text: The index is maintained by in-process event listeners, and search uses a substring query over stored content. I’m checking the entry-point differences and the limits of the rebuild path.

When someone edits an issue, `updateIssueAction` in [src/actions/issues/update-issue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/actions/issues/update-issue.ts) validates and authorizes the request, then calls `updateIssue` in [src/server/services/issue-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/server/services/issue-service.ts). The service checks organization scope and permission, reads the existing issue, rejects archived issues, and writes the update through the issue repository. It then awaits an `issue.updated` event.

At server initialization, [src/instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/instrumentation.ts) calls `registerEventHandlers` in [src/server/services/event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/server/services/event-registry.ts), which installs `registerSearchListeners` from [src/server/services/search-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/server/services/search-service.ts). The `issue.updated` listener rereads the persisted issue and calls `indexIssue`; it does not use the event’s changed fields as the searchable copy. `emit` in [src/lib/event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/lib/event-bus.ts) waits for listeners to settle, so a successful listener updates the index before the edit returns. Listener failures are reported to error sinks and do not fail the write, so this is not a transactional guarantee.

The copy is the SQLite `search_index` table, defined in [src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/server/db/schema/webhooks.ts). Each row has an ID, organization, subject kind and ID, optional project ID, content, and indexing timestamp. `indexIssue` stores the title followed by the description; `indexComment` stores the body; and `indexProject` stores the name followed by the description. `upsertSearchDocument` in [src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/server/repositories/search-repository.ts) finds the row by organization, kind and subject ID, then updates it or inserts one.

The listeners also index issue, comment and project creation and remove documents on issue or project archival and comment deletion. An issue-specific `search.reindex_requested` event rereads and indexes that issue. For bulk imports or drift, `runSearchReindexJob` in [src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/server/jobs/search-reindex-job.ts) re-upserts projects, issues and their comments for one organization. Its current implementation reads only the first page of each list, and it does not clear stale documents.

For the colleague’s search, the dialog in [src/components/domain/search/search-dialog.tsx](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/components/domain/search/search-dialog.tsx) debounces input and calls `parseSearchQuery` in [src/components/domain/search/query-syntax.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/components/domain/search/query-syntax.ts). With advanced search enabled, the parser extracts recognized `kind:`/`in:` and `project:` filters and sends the remaining text; otherwise it treats the trimmed input as text and defaults to issues. The dialog calls its `onSearch` action with a limit of 20 and displays returned hits.

`searchAction` in [src/actions/search/search.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/actions/search/search.ts) runs through `withAction` in [src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/actions/_lib/with-action.ts): `searchQuerySchema` validates the input, an actor is resolved, and errors become an `ActionResult`. The action checks `org:read`, evaluates `advanced_search`, narrows requested kinds to issues when the flag is off, and calls the search service. One edge case: if that narrowing leaves an empty kinds array, the repository interprets it as **no kind filter**, rather than no results.

`search` in `search-service.ts` checks the actor’s organization scope and `issue:read` permission, then consumes the organization’s `search:query` token bucket from [src/lib/rate-limit.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/lib/rate-limit.ts). An otherwise valid query is refused when the bucket is exhausted. It then checks the organization’s `advanced_search` flag: **any colon in the submitted query is rejected when that flag is off**, even if the colon is literal punctuation in a title. This differs from the client parser’s plain-text treatment. Schema validation, authentication, organization scope and permissions can also reject a request.

Finally, `searchDocuments` filters rows by organization, content using SQL `LIKE '%query%'`, requested kinds and optional project ID. It counts matches, orders by `indexedAt` and ID descending, and uses cursor pagination. The service converts rows to `SearchHit` values: the first content line is the title, `snippetAround` extracts context around the query, and `hrefFor` builds a subject link. This is substring matching over the stored text, not a ranked full-text engine. The full-page route in [src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/search/page.tsx](</private/tmp/bench-scratch/79f4bccd-8b50-42ee-aa3c-2a25c2588c56/src/app/(dashboard)/[orgSlug]/search/page.tsx>) takes a separate path: it loads the tenant and actor, validates the raw query, chooses kinds from the flag, and calls the same service directly.
